name: browser/monitor-page
title: Watch a page for changes
summary: Check a page for a change (price, version, status) and report the difference from last time, kept in a note.
when: Use when the user asks whether a price, version or status on a page has changed since last time.
steps: Call note action search with the page name or URL to find the note holding the last reading.
Call browser action open on the url and copy only the value being watched, such as price, version or status.
Call note action read on that note and put the old value and today's value side by side with their dates.
Use calculate for the difference, such as the percent change, so the report gives a number and not an impression.
Call note action append to add today's date, the new value and the change, so the next run has a baseline.
If no earlier note exists, call note action save with today's value and say plainly that this is the first reading.
Check that the value comes from the page body itself, not from a search snippet, before reporting any change.
If the page cannot be reached, say so plainly; otherwise report the old value, the new value, the date and the change.
next: The final answer must give the old and new value with their dates and the size of the change, or say plainly that this is the first reading.
